plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, MUU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to comply with the single-name mandate.
This plan prioritizes reducing overall portfolio risk and leverage.
It favors income and broad index exposure for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation, targeting around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and adhering to strict concentration limits. Expect lower volatility but also more modest potential returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, MUU, METU, MSFU) to small, controlled positions.
Introduce TZA as a new buy, leveraging its strong scanner score.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-scoring new setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Increase exposure to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to press working positions.
Buy TZA, a high-scoring scanner setup, to further leverage growth opportunities.
This plan uses leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs decay daily. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged names (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to near zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on generating reliable income with low drawdown.
It aims to park cash for yield rather than growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
